title: 27.1 A 3-Axis MEMS Gyroscope with 2.8ms Wake-Up Time Enabled by a 1.5µW Always-on Drive Loop
problem: MEMS gyroscopes for mobile/wearable event-driven applications must minimize always-on current for battery life while achieving fast wake-up times. Burst-mode PLL (BPLL) drive loops suffer instability from parasitic-relaxation-oscillation (PRO) effects triggered by temperature variations, causing poor wake-up reliability.
motivation: Always-on gyroscopes enable low-latency motion detection for wearables and human-machine interfaces, but current-consumption and thermal-stability trade-offs limit practical deployment.
method: A duty-cycle-automatic-optimization (DAO) technique controls parasitic-relaxation-oscillation in the drive loop by adaptively adjusting duty cycle based on temperature. The always-on loop consumes just 1.5µW while maintaining stable oscillation, enabling rapid wake-up to active measurement mode with 2.8ms response time and ±5% wake-up stability across -40 to +85°C.
key_novelty: Duty-cycle-automatic-optimization (DAO) technique suppressing parasitic-relaxation-oscillation for reliable always-on MEMS drive loops.
contributions: 2.8ms wake-up time (1.9× faster than prior 5.45ms BPLL design)
±5% wake-up time stability from -40 to +85°C (vs. prior PRO-induced instability)
1.5µW always-on consumption enabling battery-efficient standby operation
Eliminates parasitic-relaxation-oscillation problems in burst-mode PLL

metrics.other: 2.8ms wake-up time, 1.5µW always-on power, ±5% stability over temperature

baselines: Burst-mode PLL design (5.45ms wake-up, PRO instability)
Conventional always-on gyroscope drive loops (higher power)
limitations: Not discussed; gyroscope noise performance, angle random walk, and bias stability not characterized.
